topic: How do on-board storage constraints influence payload power allocation between immediate and time-tagged service prioritization?
consensus_response: On-board storage constraints significantly impact payload power allocation between immediate and time-tagged services. Immediate services require higher power allocation to ensure quick processing and transmission, while time-tagged services can tolerate lower power allocation, allowing for more flexible power allocation and potentially higher efficiency. However, time-tagged services may experience delays, affecting Quality of Service (QoS). The trade-off between immediate and time-tagged services' power allocation directly modulates the satellite's array factor and interference levels, influencing both critical and less critical service performance. This dynamic power allocation strategy must optimize between immediate service needs and network-wide performance to maintain both QoS and overall network efficiency, striking a balance that prioritizes critical services while minimizing interference.
